title: Sicilian Defense: Classical Variation
line: Both knights come out first, and the queen can join them against White's knight in the center.

steps.text: The usual Sicilian start: White pushes the king's pawn, Black answers from the side, and White pushes a second center pawn.
Black trades its side pawn for that center pawn, and both sides bring a knight out.
Bring the other knight out. It hits the knight on d4.

also.a7a6: That is the Najdorf, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Classical.
also.g7g6: That is the Dragon, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Classical.

steps.after: White's bishop aims at the pawn on f7.

steps.text: Bring the queen to b6. With the knight it hits the knight on d4, and it eyes the pawn on b2.

also.e7e6: That is also played. This lesson uses the queen first.

steps.after: The knight steps back from the center.

steps.text: Push the pawn on e7 one square. It blunts White's bishop and opens a path for your other bishop.
Bring the bishop out, so you can castle.
White's bishop hits your queen. Step back to c7, where she watches e5.
Push the pawn on a7 one square. It gets the pawn on b7 ready to push forward on the queen's side.
steps.after: This is the usual plan: Black's pawns go forward on the queen's side, away from where White's king castled.

summary: In the Classical both knights come out, the queen chases White's knight back, and pawns go forward on the queen's side.
